messages:
Aisha: Quick check
Proposal: introduce a tiny canonical gating enum in release metadata (stable / canary / experimental). Purpose: cheap resolver heuristics, simpler infra routing, and clearer telemetry.
Ben: +1 but migration is the hard bit. Lots of older SDKs only read pin/variant strings. We must avoid a hard break.
Carmen: Echoing that. Namespace it under release_headers.gating_label, but server should also emit a top-level alias (gating_label) for quick access.
Eli: Two guardrails: (1) keep enum tiny (3 values max), (2) telemetry links to routing decisions (we need routing_decision events) so canary regressions are visible.
Aisha: Concrete: enum = ["stable","canary","experimental"]. Server emits gating_label at top-level plus legacy pin_hint for a 6+6 compatibility window (6 months full dual-write, then 6 months warn-only). Add header X-Release-Gating for infra routers.
Ben: Suggest servers always emit both fields and the header. Proxies/networks can honor header immediately without SDK changes.
Carmen: Example manifest fields (flattened in accepted submission format):
model_id: openlm-xxl-v3
release_headers.gating_label: canary
release_headers.epoch: 2026-03-10
release_headers.cohort: cohort-17
pin_hint: openlm-xxl-v3-20260310  // legacy
Eli: Resolver behavior proposal:
- stable -> always prefer stable pools
- canary -> prefer canary capacity; if unavailable, fallback to stable
- experimental -> route only if caller explicitly declares experimental-allowed in request

Aisha: Also add a tenant-level override (enterprise opt-out of canaries) and a per-call allow_experimental flag.
DevOpsBot: Staging preview: rollout-metadata-v2 deployed (2026.03.14). Health: 3/3 services green.
Ben: Migration playbook (draft):
1) server emits gating_label + pin_hint + header
2) SDKs: prefer gating_label, fallback pin_hint; log mismatches
3) CLI linter: warn on mismatched fields; fail in strict mode after compatibility window
4) Gradual enforcement: enable strict gating_label checks for 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100%
Carmen: Add validation webhook to reject unknown gating_label values on manifest submissions; record audit events when rejects occur.
Eli: Telemetry specifics: emit routing_decision events with reason:"gating_label" and selected_variant; sample prompt+quality metrics for canary requests; expose per-tenant canary opt-in rates; add a canary-health dashboard.
Aisha: RFC addendum items I'm taking: enum list, compatibility windows, header name (X-Release-Gating), resolver fallback rules, tenant opt-out, telemetry contract, and linter rules. Target ship dates: server PR 2026-03-21, SDK patch 2026-04-01, lint enforcement 2026-07-01.
Ben: Any infra blockers?
NetOps: We'll need a small flag in routing service to prefer canary pools when X-Release-Gating or top-level gating_label is present. I'll open infra PR and tag @netops; ETA 3 business days.
Carmen: I'll draft the webhook + linter rules, and post a PR to the canonical manifests repo with tests for unknown values.
Aisha: One extra operational note: lint should support a local --strict-gating flag so integrators can preflight before manifests land. Also add an admin API to bulk-toggle tenant canary opt-out.
Eli: For experimentation safety: require canary cohorts to be limited by both traffic fraction and tenant_count; do not allow cohort label reuse within 90 days to avoid contamination in metrics.
Ben: Plus a final check: if gating_label and pin_hint disagree, server should prefer gating_label but surface a warning in manifest status and in audit logs.
DevOpsBot: Note: rollout smoke tests will include a scenario where X-Release-Gating: canary is set by a header and routing uses canary pool. I saw flaky behavior in one test; adding a retry in routing client.
Aisha: OK great. I'll publish the addendum in #architecture and open a short async review thread. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
